clue.text: Light and delicate insect munching grass

indicators.note: the insect is eating the grass, so the grass word ends up inside the insect word

parts.note: a fly is an insect
oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A bug delicately nibbles at a lawn on a light summer's day.
explanation.definitionFit: Floaty fabrics and dresses are light, airy and delicate in texture.

clue.text: Exterior of cell building up an insulating layer

indicators.note: the exterior of a word is its outside letters, first and last, here of cell

parts.note: building up a total is adding to it

explanation.surface: A prison cell's outer wall is being built up with insulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cladding is a covering fixed to a building's walls, often to keep heat in.

clue.text: Tom, maybe, a bloke securing a river boat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, given as an example

indicators.note: the bloke word holds the next pieces fast inside itself

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A tomcat and a man are tying up a boat on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts A and R inside MAN, after the M, giving MARAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing vessel.

clue.text: Putting piece of cake in bag, I'm merry

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Someone happily stuffs a slice of cake into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' looks like the cake going in the bag, but with 'Putting' it means an easy putt in golf. GIMME runs across baG I'M MErry.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a gimme is a putt so short that opponents concede it, so it is a piece of cake.

clue.text: Flower in bow, twirling

indicators.note: twirling turns the word for bow round so it reads the other way

parts.note: to nod is to bow the head

explanation.surface: A flower is tucked into a ribbon bow and spun round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows: the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords call a river a flower because it flows, and the Don is a British river.

clue.text: Latino, I suspect, welcoming some tobacco company's demise?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the tobacco word as a guest inside them
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: a quid is a lump of chewing tobacco

explanation.surface: A Latino man is suspected of taking a tobacco firm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' makes LIATION; 'welcoming' takes in the tobacco. The question mark flags that liquidation is a company's end, not a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquidation is the winding up of a firm, selling its assets when it fails.

clue.text: Ignominious look unfortunately confronting His Excellency, initially

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the four words just before it

explanation.surface: An ambassador receives a shameful glance at a reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His Excellency' tempts as HE, but 'initially' covers every word from 'unfortunately' on, giving UCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable or shady, close to shameful or dishonourable.

clue.text: Move slowly please around king

indicators.note: the word for please goes around the letter for king

parts.note: to tickle someone is to please or amuse them
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A request to edge carefully around a king, as in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: To trickle is to flow or move slowly in a thin stream.

clue.text: Very busy hospital, one got upset about it

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round it, the hospital letter mentioned first
upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these words are jumbled

parts.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital is frantically busy, and someone is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes ONTEGO and 'about it' wraps the hospital letter; 'it' points back to the hospital at the clue's start.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go is an idiom for being constantly active and busy.

clue.text: Bury doctor alongside mysterious note

indicators.note: something mysterious is obscure, so the letters of note are muddled

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is buried next to a cryptic message.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, that is to inter it.

clue.text: Brolly, brown, extremely smooth, in rear of car

indicators.note: the colour and letters are placed inside the car's rear

parts.note: the boot is the luggage space at the back of a British car (a trunk)
umber is a brown earth pigment

indicators.note: the extreme letters of a word are its first and last

explanation.surface: A sleek brown umbrella is kept in the back of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SH, the ends of smooth. Brolly is British slang for an umbrella.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumbershoot is a jocular old American word for an umbrella, the same as a brolly.

clue.text: Knight needing time to escape prison

indicators.note: the time letter gets out of the prison word, leaving the rest

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A knight must wait for his chance to break out of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title given to a knight.

clue.text: Artist attaching to right-wing extremes in The Bronx? Not particularly

indicators.note: the right-hand ends of the next three words, their final letters

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An artist joins far-right activists in New York, and is asked if that was wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' looks like a separate reply but is the third word, giving EXT. 'Bronx?' and 'right-wing' invite a political reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra used as an adverb, as in extra careful, means especially or unusually.

clue.text: Rough justice finally said to have claimed Mimi's heart

indicators.note: takes just the closing letter of justice
the word for said takes hold of the heart letters, enclosing them

parts.note: stated means said

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a rough punishment has taken Mimi's heart, as in the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough justice' reads as one phrase, but rough alone is the definition and justice only supplies its last letter. Mimi is the heroine of the opera La Bohème.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough figure is an approximate one, an estimated guess.

clue.text: Shoppers perhaps in America missing garters

indicators.note: the letters for America are absent from the garters word

parts.note: suspenders are British garters, straps that hold up stockings
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Shoppers in America find there are no garters for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain suspenders hold up stockings; in America the word means braces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers are people who spend money, given as one example of such spenders.

clue.text: Stop pinching flanker's rear in ruck

indicators.note: the stop word nips the letter between its ends

parts.note: to cease is to stop

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rugby referee tells a forward to stop pinching in the ruck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanker' and 'ruck' are rugby terms, but ruck here means a wrinkle or fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruck is a crumple or fold in cloth, which is a crease.

clue.text: Melt stopped by a cold front

indicators.note: the melt word is plugged by the next letters inside it

parts.note: to melt away is to fade
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A thaw is halted by an arriving cold weather front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' suggests weather, but here it is the face of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is the front face of a building, or a false front put on.

clue.text: Total dismissed twice?

definitions.meaning: complete or utter, as in a total disaster
a batsman given ... again in cricket has been dismissed twice

explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means utter or complete, and humorously out on two occasions.

clue.text: Asian behind housing problem, ultimately

indicators.note: the behind word gives a home to the letter inside it

parts.note: a tail is at the behind of an animal

indicators.note: takes the very last letter of problem

explanation.surface: An Asian person is in trouble with the housing problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so Asian.

clue.text: Was a woolly mammoth so old?

definitions.text: Was a woolly mammoth so old?

parts.words: Was a woolly mammoth so old?
parts.note: an idiom for being elderly, read literally of a huge tusked beast

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone getting old, from judging a horse's age by its teeth.

clue.text: Trail film about a termagant, primarily, opinionated type

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail them

indicators.note: the film word goes about the next letters

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass

indicators.note: takes the first letter of termagant

explanation.surface: A stubborn person trails a film about a shrewish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A termagant is a bad-tempered, overbearing woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogmatist asserts opinions as certain truth, an opinionated sort.

clue.text: Giant's description of himself, briefly: more than one foot?

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: a giant might say of himself I am big

explanation.surface: A giant's terse account of himself mentions more than one foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' tempts as a measure of the giant's size; it is a metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of short then long syllable; iambi is its plural.

clue.text: Politician, Tory leader say, in the drink

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party

indicators.note: the letter is spoken out loud, giving a word that sounds like it
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A politician and the Tory leader are thrown in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' looks like slang for the sea, as in 'in the drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is unfermented tea, a type of beverage.

clue.text: French dish in container, by the sound of it, some urn I modified

indicators.note: the container word is spoken, giving a French word that sounds the same

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware pot

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French dish served in a pot, much like an urn altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' turns SOME URN I into MONSIEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A croque monsieur is a French toasted ham and cheese sandwich.

clue.text: Conservative matched with US president

parts.note: level means equal or matched
and means together with

explanation.surface: A British Conservative is paired off with an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and 24th President of the United States.

clue.text: Relations depicted in this text?

parts.note: relations means sexual relations, not family, in an ancient Indian manual

explanation.definitionFit: The Kama Sutra is the ancient Sanskrit text on love and sexual behaviour.

clue.text: Moonshine or fruit drinks

definitions.meaning: moonshine means foolish talk or nonsense
iced drinks of wine or sherry with fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers is British slang for nonsense and also names iced fruit drinks.

clue.text: One on the fiddle in game

definitions.meaning: on a violin, the raised piece holding up the strings
a card game for four players in two partnerships

explanation.definitionFit: A bridge supports the strings of a violin, and bridge is also a card game.

clue.text: Item of headgear, little one fitted around head of rector

indicators.note: the little one word is fitted around the letter

parts.note: a mite is a small child or tiny creature

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small child's hat is fitted around a clergyman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed hat worn by bishops.

clue.text: Force in the direction of rising river

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: to ram is to force
at, as in throwing at someone, means toward

explanation.surface: A powerful current pushes towards a swelling river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar forms most of the border between Devon and Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is a river in south-west England.
